sentences.text: Wulatelong gobiensis is the only known species of this basal oviraptorid dinosaur, a bird-like theropod that lived in the Late Cretaceous of Asia.
Members of this group possessed toothless, parrot-like beaks and often featured elaborate crests, while their diets ranged from herbivorous to omnivorous.
The name Wulatelong merges the discovery site, Wulate, with the Chinese word for dragon.
A single nearly-complete skeleton cataloged as IVPP V 18409 provides the primary evidence for this animal.
The specimen was unearthed in 2009 in the Bayan Mandahu area of Inner Mongolia before the genus was formally described by Xu and colleagues in 2013.
This dinosaur shared its environment with ceratopsians such as Protoceratops and Magnirostris, the ankylosaurian Pinacosaurus, and various other theropods.
Scientists have concluded that the Bayan Mandahu fauna differs fundamentally from the classical Djadokhta fauna, possibly due to age differences or environmental factors.
Taxonomically, Wulatelong belongs to the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Sauropsida, order Saurischia, and theropod suborder Theropoda.
It is placed within the infraorder Oviraptorosauria, the superfamily Caenagnathoidea, and the subfamily Citipatinae.
This animal inhabited the Late Cretaceous Wulansuhai Formation of Inner Mongolia, China, living between 75 and 71 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
The estimated time range for Wulatelong spans from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether the difference between the Bayan Mandahu and Djadokhta faunas is due to age differences or environmental factors.
